Do not estimate a bbox from the apparent center of a cell. For each character independently, trace the outermost visible foreground pixels on all four sides. Include every visible pixel belonging to that character, including hair, hands, feet, clothing, held weapons, equipment, accessories, and antialiased edge pixels. Exclude background, shadows, and neighboring characters. After finding the observed outermost foreground pixels, expand the bbox by 3 pixels on every side, clipped to the image bounds and without including a neighbor. Different silhouettes should normally produce different bbox coordinates and dimensions; reuse identical width or height only when the independently observed pixel boundaries truly match. Before returning, verify for every item that no visible foreground pixel belonging to it lies above, below, left, or right of its bbox. If an edge cannot be determined reliably, lower confidence instead of guessing or substituting a grid-derived value. Define foot_anchor as the center of the lowest visible sole contact span belonging to the character; exclude weapons, hanging accessories, shadows, and unrelated objects from this anchor. If both feet touch the ground, use the center spanning both sole contacts. If only one foot touches, use that sole center.
